question.problem:
Find the solution to the inequality $\frac{2z+9}{3}\ge -z-1.$

The solution is $z$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $3:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2z+9}{3} & \ge -z-1 \\ 3\cdot (\frac{2z+9}{3}) & \ge 3\cdot (-z-1) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot (\frac{2z+9}{\cancel{3}}) & \ge 3\cdot (-z-1) \\ 2z+9 & \ge -3z-3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}2z+9 & \ge -3z-3 \\ 2z+9+3z & \ge -3z-3+3z \\ 5z+9 & \ge -3 \\ 5z+9-9 & \ge -3-9 \\ 5z & \ge -12 \\ \frac{5z}{5} & \ge \frac{-12}{5} \\ z & \ge -\frac{12}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z\ge -\frac{12}{5}.$
